title: Getting "LeakSanitizer: detected memory leaks" with GCC, but Valgrind shows everything ok
body_html:
I'm doing some basic tests to understand better how singly-linked-lists works in memory, as I have some doubts specific to the scope of malloc(), and why free() is not explicitly necessary in the code.

The problem starts when I compile my code, everything here seems fine, but when I run it, it shows the "LeakSanitizer: detected memory leaks" message.

I'm doing the compiling with GCC version 10.1.0

gcc linked.c -Wall -O2 -fsanitize=address -fno-omit-frame-pointer -march=skylake -flto -ggdb -o linked

Message after running my code:

==29248==ERROR: LeakSanitizer: detected memory leaks

Direct leak of 27 byte(s) in 3 object(s) allocated from:
    #0 0x7f924a2de9c7 in __interceptor_malloc (/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libasan.so.6+0xae9c7)
    #1 0x7f924b200aac in createNode /home/delok/linked.c:29
    #2 0x7f924b200aac in main /home/delok/linked.c:20
    #3 0x7f9249e51bf6 in __libc_start_main (/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6+0x21bf6)

SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: 27 byte(s) leaked in 3 allocation(s).

Something I can't understand is the fact that Valgrind tells me that everything its ok:

Valgrind command:

valgrind --leak-check=full -v ./linked

Valgrind output:

==29250==ASan runtime does not come first in initial library list; you should either link runtime to your application or manually preload it with LD_PRELOAD.

Code:

 #include <stdio.h>
 #include <stdlib.h>

 struct Node{

     unsigned short x : 5;
     struct Node *next;

 }__attribute__((packed));

 struct Node *head = NULL;

 // Definitions

 int main(void)
 {

     for(int i = 0; i <= 3; ++i)
         createNode(i);

     return 0;

 }

 void createNode(int val)
 {

     struct Node *link = (struct Node *) malloc(sizeof(struct Node));

     link->x = val;
     link->next = head;
     head = link;

     printf("Node value: %d\n", link->x);
     printf("Node Address: %p\n", link);
     printf("Pointing to : %p\n", link->next);


 }

Best,

events.body_html: The loop for(int i = 0; i <= 3; ++i) creates 4 nodes, but the sanitizer only reports 3 allocations. Note that the free() is not strictly necessary because dynamically allocated memory is handed back to the system on program exit, but it's good practice to do the housekeeping yourself.

@WeatherVane, thanks for the answer, but a few questions, following good practices, which would be the correct way to free the allocated memory? Because in every call to createNode(),  malloc will allocate memory, so how could I do the cleaning when we refer to a malloc inside a function? And as I see maybe malloc is not the correct approach in this soluction right?

malloc() is fine for this job. To free the linked list, traverse it until you reach the NULL pointer link, putting each next member into a temporary variable and free() the node memory. You need the temporary variable because the next link won't be accessible after you free() the node. Practice the traversal with a printlist() function first.

I downloaded your code and build two versions: one with -fsanitize=address (e.g. san) and one without (e.g. val). I ran valgrind on val and it complained. I ran san and it complained. When I ran valgrind on san, the libasan code complained but valgrind did not. Note that both tools want to co-opt/redirect malloc et. al. so the two tools may be mutually exclusive
@WeatherVane, Thanks, really appreciate the advice, I'll be working on this the next days, stay safe!
@CraigEstey, that's good to know, I'll be studying more the GCC flags to fully understand the compatibility between tools. Thanks!
Try building without asan then running under Valgrind.
